questions.question: The build's rules retry is skipped once 80 s have passed, and in the canonical Waltzman build the test run starts at 85-111 s. Should the cut-off, or the order of the build steps, change so the retry can repair a world?

questions.resolves_with: An argument already settles that the retry is skipped (85, 101 and 111 s against 80 s). In those runs the test run found no part-way problem, so nothing needed repair (c1r24 TRACE_READ.md:54): it is a latent risk for a world that does. questions.short: A refusal is not linked to its cause
questions.question: When an earlier move this round changes the state before a person's move, does the record say which event blocked it? On the live open-attempt path the same attempt is resubmitted at the new revision and only its rule's checks decide it (scripts/run_authored_world.py:571-573); menu paths ask once more (:581). On every path the refused row lists the failed check labels (refused_because, :622-627) but not the event that changed the state.
questions.blocks: whether a reader of a run (or the readout) can say why a person's move was refused, in any world
questions.resolves_with: An argument settles it: the run loop already knows which submitted event changed the revision before the loser's pick, so naming it costs nothing and belongs in the run loop, not any world. Build it and check on free replays of saved worlds (c1r24 Waltzman, truck) that each refused row names its blocking event id. Starting point: c1r24 call 18016 shows the round's moves but not the link.
questions.evidence: Settled by argument: the run loop holds the round's accepted events in order, so the last accepted event whose changes touch a path the refused move's failed checks read is the blocking event; naming it is run-loop bookkeeping that applies to every world. Answer: yes, add blocked_by_event to the refused row. Build work: docs/plans/open_attempt.md, 'Fixes settled by argument' (F1), checked on a free replay of the saved airfield and c1r24 worlds.

questions.evidence: Settled by argument: a notice copies the starter's words, so it cannot be more specific than they are (c1r24 round 10), and only a required field can make every remedy say what was decided. questions.question: Does the rules writer give a generated move rule a check that the way between places is open, so a walk into a wall is refused with the wall as the cause?

questions.resolves_with: Prior art in the run: generate the canonical airfield world in slice S1 and read its move mechanic; if the check is absent, fix the rules writer prompt and schema.
questions.evidence: No, then yes after a generic fix. The first generated airfield world put everyone at the one world location, had no move action, and its wall was read by no rule (evidence/open-attempt/q23/bundle.json, rules.json). Fixes: the bundle contract now offers each entity a starting place and asks for places, a move action with 'to' and 'way', and ways with a passable flag (scripts/generate_world_bundle.py); the validator refuses an unknown place (scripts/scaffold_world.py); the rules writer must check the actor is where the thing is, and is told checks have no 'or' (scripts/generate_causal_model.py). Regenerated world: walking through the brick wall fails 'the way is passable', flying from the office fails 'the aircraft is where the trainee is'; with the wall made passable in memory both succeed (evidence/open-attempt/q23/after-fix/probe.txt). Limit: a way works from its first place to its second only.

questions.short: Petri nets or TypeDB as carrier
questions.question: Petri nets already lend World Substrate their transition semantics (docs/plans/linked_process_participants.md:136): a process is close to a transition that fires when enabled with no actor, and output arcs are close to a declared write scope. Could a typed Petri net (AlgebraicPetri) or TypeDB (relations with role players) carry the rest well enough to adopt instead of the table in scripts/build_metamodel.py: guards that read arbitrary component checks over bound participants, partial observation (who notices a firing), and refusal of an attempted move with the failed check named?
questions.blocks: whether the metamodel keeps its own action-kind and attempt-reading types or adopts an outside carrier for them
questions.resolves_with: Prior art: read AlgebraicPetri's typed Petri net and TypeDB's relation/role schema and map each onto action kind, role, check, effect, process, observation and refused event. If either holds checks as guards, per-actor noticing and named refusal, adopt it as the carrier for those types; if one of the three has no counterpart, keep the own types and compose (Petri semantics for firing, own types for checks, noticing and refusal).
questions.evidence: Settled by argument: plain and typed Petri nets (AlgebraicPetri) fire a transition when its input places hold tokens, with no guard over component data; coloured Petri nets add data guards, but no Petri net models which observer notices a firing or a refusal that names its failed check; TypeDB holds typed relations with role players but runs no state-changing effects. None carries all three of guards over bound participants, per-observer noticing and named refusal, so the answer is compose: Petri semantics for firing (already lent, linked_process_participants.md:136) and the metamodel's own types for checks, noticing and refusal, which is what docs/model/METAMODEL.md records. Not material to the plan (docs/plans/open_attempt.md, Uncertainties).

Build work: docs/plans/open_attempt.md, 'Fixes settled by argument' (F6): the rules writer writes one move rule per direction; checked by regenerating the airfield world and probing both directions. Until it lands each TRACE_READ.md names a resident stuck behind a way it already used.

questions.question: Piece 3 rolls dice from hash(run_seed, event_id), while today no rule uses randomness (docs/plans/open_attempt.md:112). Where does run_seed live, do saved worlds replay unchanged, and who gives a generated person like Sam piloting 0?

questions.resolves_with: An argument settles the first two: the run loop draws run_seed once when a run starts and records it in the run record, and each roll event records its dice, so a replay reads the dice and never rolls; a world with no roll never draws, so every saved world replays unchanged (A8). The rule stays a function of state plus the recorded seed, so the invariant becomes 'no unrecorded randomness'. The third part is open: the rules writer must give people skill fields from the description ('has never flown' gives piloting 0) and the roll may read only that field. Settled in S3 by a free probe that regenerates the airfield spec and reads Sam's recorded skill.

questions.question: Declared read scopes are recorded but not enforced (AGENTS.md:21; docs/model/ODD.md:87): a hand-written rule can read a field outside its declared reads and nothing reports it. Should the Engine enforce or check read scopes?
questions.blocks: whether causal links built from declared reads are complete: F1's blocked_by_event names the event that changed what a refused move's failed checks read, and Piece 2's reactions cite parents, so an undeclared read would leave a refusal or reaction without its true cause
questions.resolves_with: Reading the compiler settles generated rules: their reads are derived from their own selector, checks and effects (_derived_reads, src/world_substrate/action_authoring.py:173), so they cannot read outside them. Open are hand-written mechanisms and reference worlds. Technical choice: a test-time state view that records each hand-written rule's actual reads and fails on an undeclared one; check with a test rule that reads an undeclared field.
